rows.query: does listening on a port break the promise that nothing leaves the laptop
rows.why_adversarial: Note's vocabulary is loopback, IPC, 127.0.0.1, offline-first; query uses port, laptop, promise, and shares no distinctive noun.

rows.query: the checker reported everything fine while the whole thing was dead
rows.why_adversarial: Note says health check, pulse, doctor, probe, theater; query says checker, reported, dead. Three sibling notes cover adjacent 'it looked fine' patterns.

rows.query: the other product we could not score side by side because it throws away the source file
rows.why_adversarial: Note is titled around 'head-to-head bench column' and 'mem0'; query avoids both and describes the shape mismatch in plain words, while two other notes own the word benchmark.

rows.query: changing the wording in the codebase changed nothing on the phones
rows.why_adversarial: Note's distinctive words are Storyblok, translationResolver, labels-en, i18n; none appear in the query, and the 'shipped but nothing changed on device' framing points hard at the OTA notes.

rows.query: the navigation app that always starts from where you are standing
rows.why_adversarial: Query avoids Waze, deep link, origin and waypoint entirely, and 'where you are standing' reads as a location-tracking query, pulling toward the GPS notes.

rows.query: the installed release refused to read the file my working copy had already upgraded
rows.why_adversarial: Note says dev tree, global install, config directory, downgrade hazard, migration; query says installed release, working copy, upgraded. The v0.16.0 note also narrates the same incident, so it competes on content.

rows.query: people learned to force past the safety check because it kept blocking real work
rows.why_adversarial: Four notes in the vault are about guards; only this one is about a guard that fires on valid work and trains people to override, and the query deliberately says safety check rather than guard.

rows.query: one driver ended up with two accounts because the country code was written differently
rows.why_adversarial: Note's title is E164 and subscriber matching; query uses country code and accounts. The driver-journey investigation narrates the same incident, so both are plausible and only one states the general rule.

rows.query: I checked a file that turned out not to be the one the pipeline actually reads
rows.why_adversarial: Three notes teach the same 'you inspected the wrong artifact' lesson in different domains; the query names none of the domains (pnpm/CI config vs helm values vs npm tarball vs template).

rows.query: notes disappeared from the remote after tidying folders
rows.why_adversarial: Note says archive moves, staging, blob, delete-without-add; query says tidying folders and disappeared. The guards note is the fix for exactly this and competes strongly.

rows.query: video would stall silently and it turned out not to be our code at all
rows.why_adversarial: Note's distinctive tokens are Mux, edgemv, 429, CDN, litix; the query names none, and four wing-chun-way notes all mention video playback.

rows.query: he kept pushing us to go higher which told us there was nobody else in the running
rows.why_adversarial: Two separate property notes record a seller agent coaching the bid upward as evidence of no rival bid; the query shares no address, city or price token with either.

rows.query: dependencies belong in the tracker's own fields, not written out in the description text
rows.why_adversarial: Note says relations, blocked-by, prose, Linear, ARG; query says tracker fields and description text. Three other Linear-preference notes are near neighbours.

rows.query: we unhooked the product version number from the thing that splits users into incompatible groups
rows.why_adversarial: Note's words are runtime, fingerprint, OTA, expo, semantic-release; the query uses none of them and describes the fragmentation consequence instead.

rows.query: the last step of the writing workflow was dropped because it stays a manual act
rows.why_adversarial: Note names the stage 'publish' and the tool Substack; query says last step, writing workflow, manual act, and the project MOC covers the same ground.

rows.query: a drop that lands on exactly the same position every time is the instrument, not the system
rows.why_adversarial: Three measurement notes all say 'do not believe the number yet'; only this one is about the rank-2 clustering that revealed a frozen gold set, and the query avoids hit@1, rank, bench and gold.

rows.query: expo location time interval does nothing on iphones
rows.why_adversarial: The superseded note's title is a near-verbatim match for the query; the current merged note only carries it as one section.

rows.query: background permissions call throws instead of returning denied
rows.why_adversarial: The superseded standalone note is titled almost exactly this; the live answer lives in a merged note whose title mentions none of it.

rows.query: how do I remove the always usage description keys from the ios plist
rows.why_adversarial: Same content lives in a superseded note whose title is the query almost word for word.

rows.query: pressing install on the plugin panel does nothing and shows no error
rows.why_adversarial: Two superseded notes each own half of this symptom and both name it in their titles; the surviving note is a generic merge.

rows.query: plugin update keeps serving the old code after I push commits
rows.why_adversarial: The superseded cache note is a title-level match; the current merged note buries it as section two of five.

rows.query: why does the same flow show up twice, once prefixed and once bare
rows.why_adversarial: A superseded note is devoted entirely to this namespacing rule; the live note holds it as a three-row table.

rows.query: uncaught json parse error on a 200 with no body
rows.why_adversarial: The superseded note's title contains 'empty 200 bodies' verbatim; the current merged note is titled only 'gotchas'.

rows.query: passing an empty base url silently reverts to the client wide one
rows.why_adversarial: The superseded note states this in its own title; two further notes own 'silent fallback' and 'same origin' respectively.

rows.query: is the transferz component library brand colour green or blue
rows.why_adversarial: The superseded note answers the question in its title; the current note absorbed it as a late section and is titled generically.

rows.query: can I copy a local build of the design system over node_modules to preview it
rows.why_adversarial: The superseded note is about consuming the prebuilt package and reads as the obvious hit; the current note contains the explicit 'never dist-sync' ruling.

rows.query: which gateway services still pass the params object positionally after the v6 bump
rows.why_adversarial: The superseded implementation plan shares nearly every content word with the live learning note, including the version and the guardrail framing.

rows.query: multi select filters started returning only the first value after the upgrade
rows.why_adversarial: The superseded array-params note is a direct topical match for this symptom; the surviving note carries the array shim as background inside a differently-titled note.

rows.query: fleet driver event coverage penalty toggle slice one
rows.why_adversarial: Two notes share the same date, ticket and almost the same filename; one is explicitly superseded by the other.

rows.query: how are trusted contacts stored for sharing a trip
rows.why_adversarial: The superseded v1 design carries 'share trip trusted contacts' in its filename and title; the current spec's data model replaced share_sessions with per-contact access codes.

rows.query: which directory should I be in before spawning agents
rows.why_adversarial: Two archived memory notes each hold half of this rule and were merged into the live one; all three describe the same permission-scope failure.

rows.query: polygon drawings on the hub map not sticking after save
rows.why_adversarial: The archived bug list describes the symptom in its own words and is a lexical match; the live note holds the diagnosed root cause and the shipped fix.

rows.query: how does the driver app decide its runtime version
rows.why_adversarial: Three notes with near-identical titles cover this; the May pipeline decision proposed the fingerprint policy and was reversed, and one of the three is a map-of-content rather than the decision.

rows.query: where does the analyzer review of the vault tool stand
rows.why_adversarial: The archived first review shares the title almost exactly and predates the current one by three months.

rows.query: wing chun way debugging session record
rows.why_adversarial: The archived note has the same date and almost the same filename; the live note says outright that it supersedes the mangled one.

rows.query: how far is each frontend app from the current versions
rows.why_adversarial: Four overlapping fleet snapshots exist; the May roadmap is described inside the June matrix as version-blind and now stale, but it is longer and lexically richer.

rows.query: which property sits on remediated ground where the pollution was sealed in rather than removed
rows.why_adversarial: Two Wormerveer houses have soil contamination; only this one has a formal sanering with an isolation layer, aftercare duty and a WKPB registration on the title.

rows.query: which one had heavily polluted garden topsoil that the paving is acting as a cap for
rows.why_adversarial: Same city, same contamination theme as the sibling note; the separating detail is untreated topsoil capped by paving versus a completed engineered sanering.

rows.query: the flat where the ground lease is only bought off until 2055
rows.why_adversarial: Five Amsterdam notes discuss erfpacht buy-off status; two of them have a fixed expiry, and only the year separates them (2055 versus 2057).

rows.query: the one where the yearly ground rent jumps roughly elevenfold at the end of the period
rows.why_adversarial: All four are erfpacht notes; only this one is not bought off at all and carries the canon jump, which is the only distinguishing particular.

rows.query: which candidate had by far the best neighbourhood score but failed the tenure rule
rows.why_adversarial: Many property notes carry a livability figure and several fail the tenure gate; only one has both the top score and the failing lease.

rows.query: which one did we actually bid on even though the area score was under our own minimum
rows.why_adversarial: Two Amsterdam flats score 4 on livability and both are discussed against the gate; only one had the gate flexed and a bid submitted.

rows.query: which seller disclosed damp and cracking in a bedroom on the questionnaire
rows.why_adversarial: Three notes discuss damp: one has a clean questionnaire explicitly contrasted with this one, one has hidden-moisture cover-ups, one has souterrain damp risk. Only this one has a declared bedroom defect.

rows.query: the building where the entrance hall is shared with a hotel
rows.why_adversarial: Several notes describe an awkward VvE composition (mixed rental blocks, a large corporation stakeholder, high service costs); only one has a commercial hotel co-owner in the two-tier association.

rows.query: which portal crashed because the vessel field helper threw on a null hub type
rows.why_adversarial: Five same-day plans with almost identical structure and vocabulary; the backoffice plan explicitly states the vessel helper does not exist in its codebase, which is exactly the confusable detail.

rows.query: which app's graphql returned hub as a boolean rather than an object
rows.why_adversarial: All five plans talk about originLocation.hub; only one has the data-shape mismatch where hub is a boolean and the details live under hubData.

rows.query: which migration plan was about removing wrong airport icon defaults from the dashboard
rows.why_adversarial: Icon derivation from hubType appears in three of the four portal plans, but only one treats the airport default as the thing to remove rather than as already safe.

rows.query: which one had a hub name read without optional chaining as its real crash site
rows.why_adversarial: Each portal plan lists crash sites in the same format; the separating particular is which file and which unguarded property access.

rows.query: which driver investigation traced empty lists to an unwrapped parallel fan out in the bff
rows.why_adversarial: Four notes cover journeys not reaching the driver app within two days of each other, and one of them is a learning note about the same fan-out pattern.

rows.query: which one was about gps updates failing fleet wide with an authentication rejection
rows.why_adversarial: Two notes share the same date and both are about auth failures on driver requests; only one is about the position write path returning 401 on every tick.

rows.query: which ticket needed a second stored marker so the notification would not swallow the full screen confirmation
rows.why_adversarial: Four ARG notes all discuss driver notifications and status changes; the separating detail is the interaction between two persisted keys, which is described from both sides in two of them.

rows.query: which one found that replayed buffered positions still fire the server side geofence
rows.why_adversarial: The discovery note owns the geofencing vocabulary and the production counters; only the offline note establishes that stale replayed points transition journeys with no staleness guard.

rows.query: which ticket added the persistent status strip that replaced the header row
rows.why_adversarial: Two notes discuss the banner and its copy, and the Storyblok note is where the banner wording problem was actually diagnosed, so the copy question pulls the wrong way.

rows.query: which session shipped the offline fallback page and the hand written service worker
rows.why_adversarial: Two session notes carry the same date; another one covers the PWA login loop fix, so 'PWA' alone does not separate them.

rows.query: which session added the announcements feature and the email send path
rows.why_adversarial: Same-day sibling note plus a feature note that also covers flags and a full mzyx pipeline run; the announcement particular is the only separator.

rows.query: which sso note explains that signing out leaves the session alive
rows.why_adversarial: Five SSO notes all discuss the cookie-owning edge; only one records that a token-gated logout never calls revoke in cookie mode.

rows.query: which sso document flagged the unvalidated redirect target on the deny path
rows.why_adversarial: The OAuth manual describes the same redirect_uri machinery in more detail and the loopback-allowlist note is about redirect validation too; only the review states the open-redirect finding.

rows.query: the most recent plan for making recall quality trustworthy
rows.why_adversarial: Five recall-quality plans span April to August, and the older ones use the words recall, bench and hit@1 far more heavily than the newest.

rows.query: the first time keyword and vector search were combined in the vault tool
rows.why_adversarial: The follow-up note carries the same date and the same RRF vocabulary; only one of the two is the original shipping plan.

rows.query: what did we think about the retrieval imbalance immediately after hybrid shipped
rows.why_adversarial: Two same-day notes, one shipping and one follow-up, both containing the same tables; the query turns on which came second.

rows.query: the earliest snapshot of which repos use which package manager
rows.why_adversarial: The June matrix carries a manager column too and is more recent and richer; the query asks for the earliest, not the best.

rows.query: which property was the front runner before the one we ended up buying
rows.why_adversarial: Two properties held the lead at different points and both were killed on 2026-07-20; the note that calls itself 'the current leader' is the older claim and the winner is a third note.

rows.query: the newest lesson about whether to believe a benchmark movement
rows.why_adversarial: Three measurement notes were written within a week of each other and cross-reference one another; only the dates separate them.

rows.query: the first of the driver journey investigations
rows.why_adversarial: Four notes within two days share almost all vocabulary; two carry the same later date.

rows.query: the latest of the driver notification tickets
rows.why_adversarial: Five notification-related notes span July to August, and the oldest one has the richest notification vocabulary and the longest body.

rows.query: what did we decide about the release pipeline back in may
rows.why_adversarial: The audit note carries the same date and the same project, and the August policy note answers the same question for the present, so recency bias points the wrong way.

rows.query: the older of the two trip sharing specs
rows.why_adversarial: Inverts the usual pull: the superseded note is the correct answer here, and three newer siblings from the same week are the wrong ones.

rows.query: what did the very first plan for the knowledge cli set out to do
rows.why_adversarial: A dozen metalmind plans span April to August and later ones are longer and richer; the original v1 plan is the only one that predates the product analysis written a day after it.

rows.query: the host port that came after codex
rows.why_adversarial: The query names codex, which appears in the titles of the two wrong answers and nowhere in the right one.

rows.query: what did the vault sync design settle on most recently
rows.why_adversarial: The two sync notes are two days apart, the older one states the requirements and the newer one records which of them were actually implemented and which was deliberately demoted.

rows.query: the current guidance on how a consumer app should take design system changes
rows.why_adversarial: Five transkit notes overlap heavily; the superseded one is titled around consuming the package, which is closer to the query's surface form.

rows.query: how did the house search stand at the end
rows.why_adversarial: About twenty individual property notes each end with their own status line; only the map-of-content holds the ranking as of the final date, and it is much shorter than any of them.

rows.query: what are we deliberately not building in the first version of the investment app
rows.why_adversarial: Two project notes carry a literal cuts list, and a system that ignores 'not' will match the built-features half of the same note.

rows.query: what got cut from the personal site's first release
rows.why_adversarial: The build plan and the synod note both cover the same project and the same round of decisions; only the map-of-content carries the do-not-build list.

rows.query: which stage was removed from the essay workflow
rows.why_adversarial: The note enumerates five kept stages and one dropped one; ignoring 'removed' returns the pipeline description rather than the cut.

rows.query: the typescript library we evaluated and turned down for the fleet
rows.why_adversarial: The candidates and roadmap notes are full of libraries we did adopt; the rejected one is the answer and shares all the same adoption vocabulary.

rows.query: the analytics vendor we wired up and then removed
rows.why_adversarial: The note's title and body are dominated by the vendor that stayed; the rejected one appears in one clause, and another note owns the feature-flag vocabulary outright.

rows.query: the frontend standard the council said not to make mandatory
rows.why_adversarial: Four notes describe the same tool enthusiastically; only one carries the do-not-adopt verdict, and it is the shortest of them on tool detail.

rows.query: is refusing the always on location permission actually a blocker for continuous tracking
rows.why_adversarial: The answer is no, and four sibling notes describe the permission tiers and their restrictions in detail, so a system reading the query as 'what does background permission require' returns the wrong one.

rows.query: which retrieval signal was deliberately left out of the confidence calculation
rows.why_adversarial: The excluded leg is BM25, and the hybrid-retrieval plan is entirely about adopting BM25, so ignoring 'left out' returns the opposite note.

rows.query: which house did we abandon because the ground was measurably sinking
rows.why_adversarial: Four Zaanstreek notes discuss peat soil and foundation risk; only one has a monitoring report qualifying settlement as large, and the winning property cites it as a contrast.

rows.query: which one was dropped because the repair paperwork was for the neighbour's number
rows.why_adversarial: The sibling kill note shares the city, the era and the foundation vocabulary; the separator is that here the restoration evidence exists but for the wrong address.

rows.query: the existing switch we refused to reuse for the relaxation
rows.why_adversarial: Three flag notes exist; only one is about rejecting an existing flag in favour of a dedicated one, and the rejected flag is named in a single clause.

rows.query: why we chose not to put a model in that release automation
rows.why_adversarial: The note's own section is titled around the absence of an agent, while two neighbouring notes own the Notion-publishing vocabulary that the query's surface most resembles.

rows.query: why the flow only runs in one direction
rows.why_adversarial: Three notes reject bidirectional sync for the same reason (two writable stores); the query gives no domain, and the strongest lexical match on 'sync' is the vault note.

rows.query: the one thing teammates must stop short of doing at the end of their work
rows.why_adversarial: Five agent-behaviour memories overlap; the query never names pull requests, and the sibling notes are about spawning, models and lifecycle rather than the terminal state.

rows.query: what should I stop doing right after pushing a branch
rows.why_adversarial: The sibling memory tells you to verify the deploy job, which is the opposite instruction, and both are about CI runs after a push.

rows.query: the kind of output I am never supposed to produce for analysis
rows.why_adversarial: Several style and safety memories constrain output; only this one bans publishing an artifact, and the query avoids artifact, publish and web page.

rows.query: what kind of native change does not force a new store build
rows.why_adversarial: Expo's own rule is that any native change forces a bump, so the whole vault's surrounding vocabulary argues for the wrong answer; only this note states the exception.

rows.query: the component that does not exist in the design system even though people keep reaching for it
rows.why_adversarial: The superseded note is titled after the missing component and is the obvious lexical hit; the inventory note lists components that do exist, which is the other direction of the negation.

rows.query: the pipeline redesign that was written up and then never actually built
rows.why_adversarial: The note reads as a set of firm decisions and only a late banner records that it was never implemented and was reversed on the merits; the audit that prompted it shares the date.

rows.query: what do we leave out of a ticket description on purpose
rows.why_adversarial: Four Linear-process memories compete; only this one enumerates what must not appear (acceptance criteria by default, file paths, relations as prose).

rows.query: why the browser side check is not where the real enforcement lives
rows.why_adversarial: Four SSO notes discuss client-side gating; only one states that the frontend gate is not the security boundary and that the mint endpoint checks nothing.
